subject: general
question: Which statistical indicator is used to measure the depth of poverty by accounting for the extent to which individuals fall below the poverty line?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Poverty Gap Index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Poverty Gap Index** measures the intensity of poverty by calculating the average shortfall of incomes of the poor relative to the poverty line.
 
• It highlights the depth of poverty by determining how far individuals fall below the poverty line on average.
 
• The Poverty Gap Index is expressed as a proportion of the poverty line, making it a useful tool for comparing poverty across different regions or countries.
 
• A higher Poverty Gap Index indicates deeper poverty, showing that the poor are further away from the poverty threshold.
 
• This index is widely used in socio-economic studies for policy formulation aimed at poverty alleviation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gini Coefficient:**

 
 
• A measure of income inequality within a population, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality).
 
• It does not account for poverty depth or distribution below the poverty line.
 
 
 
• **Headcount Ratio:**
 
 
• Represents the proportion of the population living below the poverty line.
 
• It is a simple measure but does not provide information about the intensity or depth of poverty.
 
 
 
• **Dependency Ratio:**
 
 
• The ratio of dependents (people aged below 15 and above 64) to the working-age population.
 
• It is used to analyze demographic and economic burdens but is unrelated to poverty measurement.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Poverty Metrics:**
 
 
• Poverty metrics like the Poverty Gap Index help policymakers design targeted interventions for poverty reduction.
 
• They provide insights into not just the prevalence but also the severity of poverty.
